id: lost-laptop.md::intro
text:
Lost or stolen laptop — read this first
**Report it first, look for it second.** Everything else on this page can wait;
that can't. Reporting takes thirty seconds and is reversible — if you find the
laptop in your other bag an hour later, nothing is lost. An unreported laptop
sitting in a taxi for a day is a different problem entirely.

Nobody is in trouble for losing a laptop. It happens several times a year at
any company. The only thing that makes it worse is waiting.
heading: read this first

id: lost-laptop.md::I've lost my laptop
text:
Lost or stolen laptop — I've lost my laptop
1. **Post in #it-help now.** Say: lost laptop, roughly where and when, and
   whether you think it was stolen. Don't wait until you've finished
   searching.
2. **If it's outside working hours, call the on-call number** in your welcome
   pack rather than posting. Out of hours, a Slack message may sit unread until
   morning — which is exactly the window that matters.
3. **Then go and look for it.** Retrace your route, call the venue, check lost
   property. Most laptops turn up.

Once you've reported it, we lock it remotely and sign it out of your accounts.
That happens whether or not the laptop is switched on — the moment it next
connects to the internet, it locks.
heading: I've lost my laptop

id: lost-laptop.md::It's been stolen
text:
Lost or stolen laptop — It's been stolen
If your laptop was stolen, nicked, taken, or robbed — from a bag, a car, a cafe
table —
the first move is the same as a loss: **post in #it-help immediately** (or call
the on-call number out of hours) and say clearly that it was stolen rather than
mislaid, because we treat the two differently. We'll lock it remotely straight
away.

Then:

1. **Report it to the police** and get a crime reference number. In the UK you
   can do this online at [police.uk](https://www.police.uk) — you don't need to
   attend a station.
2. **Send the reference number to IT.** We need it for insurance, and if it's a
   work-related theft the company handles that side, not you.
3. **If it was taken with your phone**, tell us that too. Losing both at once
   means your 2FA codes are gone as well, and we'll deal with that first so you
   can still get into your accounts.
heading: It's been stolen

id: lost-laptop.md::I might get it back — do I still report it?
text:
Lost or stolen laptop — I might get it back — do I still report it?
Yes. Report it, then keep looking.

Reporting is not a decision you can't undo. If it turns up, we unlock it in a
couple of minutes and you carry on. There's no paperwork, no incident, no
follow-up meeting.

The question worth asking yourself isn't "will I probably find it" — it's "am I
certain nobody else could have picked it up in the meantime."
heading: I might get it back — do I still report it?

id: lost-laptop.md::What happens after I report it
text:
Lost or stolen laptop — What happens after I report it
1. We lock the laptop and sign it out of email, Slack, Drive and everything
   else. Your accounts stay yours — it's the device that's cut off, not you.
2. We check whether anything was accessed after you lost it. Usually nothing
   was.
3. We arrange a replacement. If you're in the office there's usually a spare
   the same day; remote, it's a courier and typically two working days.
4. Your files are fine. Everything in Google Drive is on the server, not the
   laptop.

Anything saved only to your Desktop or Downloads and never opened in Drive is
the one thing that may not survive. That's worth knowing now rather than
later — it's the reason we ask people to work out of Drive.
heading: What happens after I report it

id: lost-laptop.md::I found it
text:
Lost or stolen laptop — I found it
Post in #it-help and we'll unlock it. Bring it in — or if you're remote, we'll
do it on a call.

Before you use it again, tell us where you found it. If it was somewhere out
of your control for a while (a taxi, a bar, a train's lost property), we'll
wipe and reinstall it before you carry on. That's not a punishment or a
judgement about you — it's that we can't tell from the outside whether anything
was plugged into it while it was gone, and reinstalling takes an hour while
finding out the hard way takes considerably longer.
heading: I found it

id: meeting-room-screens.md::intro
text:
Meeting room screens — read this first
Every room has the same kit: a screen, a USB-C cable on the table, a camera
above the screen, and an iPad by the door.
heading: read this first

id: meeting-room-screens.md::The screen won't connect — I plugged in and it's black (HDMI or USB-C)
text:
Meeting room screens — The screen won't connect — I plugged in and it's black (HDMI or USB-C)
Work down the list — it's almost always step 1 or 2.

1. **Check the screen is awake.** Tap the iPad by the door. If the screen was
   asleep it takes about ten seconds to come up. Wait for it before assuming
   the cable is the problem.
2. **Push the cable in properly.** The USB-C connector needs a firm push — a
   loose one gives you power but no picture, so a charging laptop is not proof
   it's seated.
3. **Try the other end.** Unplug from your laptop, count to five, plug back in.
   This fixes it more often than it should.
4. **Check you're not on the wrong input.** On the iPad, tap **Share screen**.
   If it's already highlighted, tap it off and on again.
5. **Try the spare cable.** Each room has a second cable in the drawer under
   the screen, plus an HDMI adapter if your laptop only has an HDMI lead. If
   the spare works, leave the broken one on the table and tell us — don't put
   it back in the drawer.

Still black after all five: move rooms if people are waiting, then post in
#it-help with the room name. Getting the room name saves us ten minutes.
heading: The screen won't connect — I plugged in and it's black (HDMI or USB-C)

id: meeting-room-screens.md::The screen works but there's no sound
text:
Meeting room screens — The screen works but there's no sound
Your Mac is still playing sound through its own speakers.

1. Hold **Option** and click the speaker icon in the top-right of your screen.
2. Under **Output Device**, choose the room's screen — it'll be named after
   the room, e.g. **Boardroom**.
3. If the room isn't listed, unplug the cable and plug it back in, then check
   again.

If you're in a video call, do this too: in Zoom or Google Meet, click the arrow
next to the microphone icon and set **Speaker** to the room as well. The Mac
setting and the call setting are separate, which is why sound sometimes works
in music but not in the meeting.
heading: The screen works but there's no sound

id: meeting-room-screens.md::I can't see the room camera in Zoom or Google Meet
text:
Meeting room screens — I can't see the room camera in Zoom or Google Meet
The camera is a separate device from the screen and has to be picked manually.

1. In **Zoom**: click the arrow next to the video icon → choose the camera
   named after the room.
2. In **Google Meet**: click the three dots → **Settings** → **Video** →
   choose the room camera.
3. If the room camera isn't in the list, your laptop hasn't seen it yet.
   Unplug the USB-C cable, wait five seconds, plug it back in, then check
   again.
4. Still not there — quit Zoom or your browser completely and reopen it. Some
   apps only look for cameras when they start.
heading: I can't see the room camera in Zoom or Google Meet

id: meeting-room-screens.md::Someone else is showing and I need to swap
text:
Meeting room screens — Someone else is showing and I need to swap
You don't need them to unplug first.

1. Plug your own cable in.
2. On the iPad, tap **Share screen**. It switches to you.

If the room has two cables on the table, both can stay plugged in — the iPad
decides who's showing.
heading: Someone else is showing and I need to swap

id: meeting-room-screens.md::The room iPad is frozen
text:
Meeting room screens — The room iPad is frozen
1. Hold the button on the top edge until you see the power slider, drag it
   across, wait ten seconds, then hold the same button to switch it back on.
   It takes about a minute to come back.
2. While it restarts, you can still share by plugging in directly — the screen
   usually switches on its own.
3. If it comes back and still won't respond, post in #it-help with the room
   name and carry on with the meeting. Don't unplug anything behind the screen.
heading: The room iPad is frozen

id: meeting-room-screens.md::Nothing here worked and the meeting starts in two minutes
text:
Meeting room screens — Nothing here worked and the meeting starts in two minutes
Move to another room if one's free, or dial in from your laptop with headphones
and share your screen that way. Fix it after, not during — post in #it-help
with the room name and what you tried, and we'll get to it before the next
booking.
heading: Nothing here worked and the meeting starts in two minutes

id: new-joiner-setup.md::intro
text:
New joiner: setting up your Mac — read this first
Welcome. This should take about 45 minutes. You don't need to finish it all
before your first meeting — get through "day one" and come back to the rest.
heading: read this first

id: new-joiner-setup.md::Day one: what to do first
text:
New joiner: setting up your Mac — Day one: what to do first
Do these four in order. Each one depends on the last.

1. **Turn the Mac on and follow the setup screens.** When it asks you to sign
   in, use your work Google account (the `@company.com` one in your welcome
   email), not a personal Apple ID.
2. **Set a password you'll remember.** You'll type this several times a day.
   It must be at least 12 characters. A short phrase with a number in it works
   well and is easier to live with than something random.
3. **Connect to Wi-Fi.** Click the Wi-Fi icon top-right and join **Office-5G**.
   The password is on the card in your welcome pack, or ask anyone sitting near
   you — it's not a secret.
4. **Open Company Portal** (it's already installed, in your Applications
   folder). Sign in with your work account. This is what installs everything
   else, so nothing below will work until you've done this.

Once Company Portal says "You're all set", the standard apps start installing
by themselves. It takes about twenty minutes. You can keep using the laptop
while it happens.
heading: Day one: what to do first

id: new-joiner-setup.md::How do I get the apps I need?
text:
New joiner: setting up your Mac — How do I get the apps I need?
Open **Company Portal** and browse the list. Click **Install** on anything you
need — no approval, no ticket, no waiting.

You'll get these automatically without asking: Chrome, Slack, 1Password, Zoom,
Google Drive, Notion.
heading: How do I get the apps I need?

id: new-joiner-setup.md::The app I need for my job isn't in the list
text:
New joiner: setting up your Mac — The app I need for my job isn't in the list
Some tools are paid per-person, so they're not installed by default. Post in
#it-help with the app name and one line on what you need it for. That line
isn't a test — it's so we buy the right licence tier.

Don't download it from the internet yourself, even if there's a free version.
That's how two people end up on different versions and nothing lines up.
heading: The app I need for my job isn't in the list

id: new-joiner-setup.md::Setting up 1Password
text:
New joiner: setting up your Mac — Setting up 1Password
1Password stores every work password so you only have to remember your Mac one.

1. Open **1Password** and choose **Sign in with your work account**.
2. Accept the invite in your email if it asks for one.
3. Install the browser extension when it offers — this is the part that makes
   it actually useful, because it fills passwords in for you.

Everything shared with the whole company lives in the **Everyone** vault: the
Wi-Fi password, the printer, shared logins.
heading: Setting up 1Password

id: new-joiner-setup.md::I don't have access to something I need
text:
New joiner: setting up your Mac — I don't have access to something I need
Access isn't automatic for everything — some tools are granted per team.

Post in #it-help with the tool name and what you're trying to do. Most things
are granted the same day.

If it's during your first week and something's obviously missing (no email, no
Slack, no calendar), that's a setup problem rather than a permissions one —
say so and we'll treat it as urgent.
heading: I don't have access to something I need

id: new-joiner-setup.md::Something's gone wrong and I'm stuck
text:
New joiner: setting up your Mac — Something's gone wrong and I'm stuck
You won't break anything by asking. Post in #it-help with:

- what you were trying to do
- what happened instead
- a screenshot if there's an error message

That's genuinely all we need. New-joiner setup problems are common and usually
five minutes to fix.
heading: Something's gone wrong and I'm stuck

id: passwords-and-logins.md::I can't get into 1Password
text:
Passwords and logins — I can't get into 1Password
1. Check you're using your **work** account, not a personal one. If you had
   1Password before joining, the app may be opening your personal vault —
   click your account name at the top and switch.
2. If it's asking for a **Secret Key** you don't have, that's in the email
   1Password sent when your account was created. Search your inbox for
   "1Password Emergency Kit".
3. Can't find that email — post in #it-help and we'll send a new invite. We
   can't recover your existing one, but a fresh invite gets you back in.

Don't reset 1Password by creating a new account. You'll end up with an empty
vault and lose access to everything shared with you.
heading: I can't get into 1Password

id: passwords-and-logins.md::I've forgotten my Mac password
text:
Passwords and logins — I've forgotten my Mac password
We can't look this up — it's stored on your laptop, not on a server. But we
can get you back in.

1. Restart the Mac. At the login screen, wait a few seconds and it should
   offer **Reset it using your Apple ID** or a question mark by the password
   box. If your Mac is set up with your work Google account, follow that
   prompt.
2. If nothing appears, bring the laptop to IT. Don't try guessing repeatedly —
   after several attempts it locks for progressively longer.
3. If you're remote, post in #it-help and we'll book fifteen minutes on a
   call. It's fixable, it just needs a person.
heading: I've forgotten my Mac password

id: passwords-and-logins.md::A site is asking for a 6-digit code and I don't have it
text:
Passwords and logins — A site is asking for a 6-digit code and I don't have it
That's two-factor authentication. The code lives in 1Password, not your text
messages.

1. Open **1Password** and find the login for that site.
2. Look for a field called **one-time password**. The 6-digit code is there
   and changes every thirty seconds.
3. Copy it and paste it in quickly — if it expires, wait for the next one
   rather than reusing the old one.

If there's no such field on that login, 2FA was probably set up on your phone
instead. Check your Authenticator app.
heading: A site is asking for a 6-digit code and I don't have it

id: passwords-and-logins.md::I've lost my phone and can't get my 2FA codes
text:
Passwords and logins — I've lost my phone and can't get my 2FA codes
Post in #it-help and say clearly that it's a 2FA lockout. This one we treat as
urgent, because it locks you out of everything at once.

Have your laptop with you when we get to you — the fastest fix uses a session
that's already signed in, before it expires.
heading: I've lost my phone and can't get my 2FA codes

id: passwords-and-logins.md::I think someone else has my password
text:
Passwords and logins — I think someone else has my password
Tell us straight away in #it-help, before you try to fix it yourself.

Say what you think happened — clicked a link, typed it into a site that looked
wrong, shared it with someone. Nobody is in trouble for reporting this. Every
company deals with it, and the only version that causes real damage is the one
nobody mentions for a week.

While you wait for us:

1. Change that password in 1Password if you can still get in.
2. Don't delete the suspicious email or message — we'll want to see it to
   check whether anyone else got the same one.
heading: I think someone else has my password

id: passwords-and-logins.md::How do I make a good password?
text:
Passwords and logins — How do I make a good password?
Let 1Password generate it. That's the whole answer — click the field, choose
**Generate password**, save it.

The only password you should ever create yourself is your Mac login, since
that's the one you type from memory. Three or four unrelated words with a
number is both stronger and easier to remember than a short jumble of symbols.
heading: How do I make a good password?

id: wifi-and-vpn.md::I can't find the office Wi-Fi network
text:
Wi-Fi and VPN — I can't find the office Wi-Fi network
1. Click the Wi-Fi icon in the top-right of your screen.
2. Look for **Office-5G**. If you only see **Office-Guest**, you're on the
   visitor network — it works, but it's slower and blocks some internal tools.
3. Can't see **Office-5G** at all? Turn Wi-Fi off, wait five seconds, turn it
   back on. It usually reappears.
4. Still nothing after that — post in #it-help. You may not be on the network
   allowlist yet, and we have to add you manually.
heading: I can't find the office Wi-Fi network

id: wifi-and-vpn.md::My Wi-Fi keeps dropping
text:
Wi-Fi and VPN — My Wi-Fi keeps dropping
This is almost always one of three things. Work down the list.

1. **You're on the wrong network.** Click the Wi-Fi icon and check you're on
   **Office-5G**, not **Office-Guest**. Guest drops connections by design.
2. **Your Mac is clinging to a weak signal.** Hold the Option key and click the
   Wi-Fi icon — you'll see extra detail. If **RSSI** is worse than -70, you're
   too far from an access point. Move rooms and see if it settles.
3. **The connection is stale.** Click the Wi-Fi icon → Wi-Fi Settings → find
   **Office-5G** → click the three dots → **Forget This Network**. Then join it
   again with the password from 1Password.

If it still drops after all three, tell us in #it-help *which* of these you
tried and where you were sitting. That saves us twenty minutes.
heading: My Wi-Fi keeps dropping

id: wifi-and-vpn.md::I need the Wi-Fi password
text:
Wi-Fi and VPN — I need the Wi-Fi password
It's in 1Password, in the **Everyone** vault, under **Office Wi-Fi**.

If you can't get into 1Password, that's the real problem — see the
passwords and logins guide.
heading: I need the Wi-Fi password

id: wifi-and-vpn.md::I'm working from home and can't reach an internal tool
text:
Wi-Fi and VPN — I'm working from home and can't reach an internal tool
Some tools only accept connections from the office network or the VPN.
If a link works in the office and not at home, you need the VPN on.

1. Open **Tailscale** from the menu bar at the top of your screen.
2. If it says *Disconnected*, click **Connect**.
3. Wait for it to say *Connected*, then reload the page.
heading: I'm working from home and can't reach an internal tool

id: wifi-and-vpn.md::The VPN says connected but nothing loads
text:
Wi-Fi and VPN — The VPN says connected but nothing loads
1. Click **Disconnect**, wait ten seconds, click **Connect** again. This fixes
   it most of the time.
2. If it doesn't: quit Tailscale completely (right-click the menu bar icon →
   Quit), reopen it, and connect again.
3. Still stuck — check whether a normal website like google.com loads. If that
   fails too, the problem is your home internet, not the VPN.
heading: The VPN says connected but nothing loads

id: wifi-and-vpn.md::I'm being asked to log into the VPN again and again
text:
Wi-Fi and VPN — I'm being asked to log into the VPN again and again
Your session has expired, which is normal and happens every 30 days.
Sign in with your Google work account. If the login window won't appear at
all, restart your Mac — it's a known glitch and a restart clears it.
heading: I'm being asked to log into the VPN again and again
